steps.do: Install vue-i18n version 9 as a runtime dependency.

Create src/i18n/index.ts that calls createI18n with legacy set to false, locale en, fallbackLocale en, and messages containing en.
In src/main.ts, import i18n from ./i18n and call app.use(i18n) before app.mount.

K-018503.example: Running npm install vue-i18n@9 adds the package, then createI18n({ legacy: false, locale: 'en', fallbackLocale: 'en', messages: { en } }) in src/i18n/index.ts exposes t through useI18n(). The file src/main.ts then calls app.use(i18n) before app.mount('#app').

Do not call $tc, which was removed in vue-i18n v9; use t with a count argument instead.
Do not skip app.use(i18n), because every t call then throws at runtime.

steps.do: Create the test file test/form_rebuild_test.dart.

In the test, call tester.enterText five times with strings that grow by one character each time, and call await tester.pump after each call.
Assert expect(buildCount, 5) so the test fails if the form rebuilds more than once per keystroke.
Run only this test file to get the rebuild assertion result.

K-018534.example: Typing 'h', 'he', 'hel', 'hell', 'hello' into a LoginForm wrapper gives buildCount 5 after the loop, which matches one rebuild per keystroke. If the count reads 10, the parent is calling setState on both the change and the focus event.
K-018534.check: The output ends with 'All tests passed!' and the expect(buildCount, 5) assertion passes.
traps: Counting builds on the root MaterialApp instead of the form subtree gives false numbers.
Forgetting await tester.pump after enterText means the rebuild has not run yet, so the count is too low.

steps.do: Create the golden directory test/goldens for the form screenshots.
Write a testWidgets case that sets tester.view.physicalSize to 400 by 800 and calls expectLater with matchesGoldenFile to the file login_form.png.
Generate the baseline PNG on the first run with the update flag.
Run the same test again without the update flag so Flutter compares pixels against the baseline.
Record the SHA-256 of the baseline image so any later change to the file is visible.

K-018535.example: LoginForm at 400 by 800 writes test/goldens/login_form.png, and a later run where the error text color changes fails with 'Pixel test failed' and a diff image. The recorded hash changes from the stored value only when the golden was regenerated.
K-018535.check: The second flutter test run prints 'All tests passed!' and the sha256sum output matches the hash stored in the review notes.
traps: Running --update-goldens on every run hides real regressions, so use it only after a deliberate visual change.
Goldens made on macOS can fail on Linux CI because font rendering differs, and a missing fixed view size makes the image depend on the host window.

steps.do: Create the integration test file integration_test/form_perf_test.dart.
In the test, wrap 20 pump calls that type into 12 fields inside binding.traceAction so the timeline records those frames.
Create the driver file test_driver/perf_driver.dart that calls integrationDriver with a timeline summary writer.
Run the timeline on a connected device or emulator in profile mode, because debug builds are too slow to compare.
Read average_frame_build_time_millis from the summary JSON and compare it with 16.

K-018536.example: After typing into 12 fields across 20 frames, the summary shows average_frame_build_time_millis of 4.2, which is under the 16ms budget. A value of 19.8 means the form is dropping frames at 60fps and the field builders need to be split.
K-018536.check: jq prints a number below 16 and the flutter drive command ends with 'All tests passed!'.
traps: Using flutter test instead of flutter drive gives no real timeline, so the number is meaningless.
Averaging over one or two frames is noise, so pump at least 20 frames before reading the summary.

steps.do: List every line in lib/forms that mentions TextEditingController to see where controllers are created.
Count the controller mentions per file to get the create count.
Count the dispose mentions per file to get the dispose count.
Fix any file where the dispose count is lower than the create count by adding dispose calls in the State dispose method.
Run the analyzer on the forms folder to catch unused or invalid controller code.

K-018537.example: rg -c reports login_form.dart:4 and dispose:4, so that file is balanced, but signup_form.dart:3 with dispose:2 shows one leaked controller. After adding the missing dispose call, signup_form.dart shows dispose:3.
K-018537.check: For every file, the create count equals the dispose count, and flutter analyze prints 'No issues found!'.
traps: Comments that mention TextEditingController inflate the create count, so check the actual lines.
A dispose call inside a conditional branch can be skipped, and a passing render does not prove the controller was disposed.

steps.do: List each TextFormField and InputDecoration in lib/forms to find widgets that build on every frame.
Add the const keyword to each InputDecoration, OutlineInputBorder, and EdgeInsets literal that uses only compile-time values.
Enable the prefer_const_constructors rule in analysis_options.yaml under linter rules.
Run the analyzer on the forms folder and expect zero issues.
Run the form test group to confirm const changes did not break behavior.

K-018538.example: InputDecoration(border: OutlineInputBorder()) becomes const InputDecoration(border: OutlineInputBorder()) in login_form.dart. The analyzer count drops from 7 prefer_const_constructors infos to 0, and the form tests still pass.
K-018538.check: dart analyze lib/forms prints 'No issues found!' and flutter test test/forms prints 'All tests passed!'.
traps: Adding const to a constructor that reads a variable, such as a theme value, is a compile error.
Setting the lint to info only hides it in CI, so make it a warning or error to see the count.

steps.do: Create the test file test/validation_debounce_test.dart.
Write a test using fakeAsync that types five characters with 50ms gaps and increments a validatorCalls counter inside the validator.
Call async.elapse with Duration(milliseconds: 250) and assert validatorCalls is 0, then elapse 100 more milliseconds and assert validatorCalls is 1.
Run the debounce test file by itself.
Run the whole forms test folder to catch regressions from the timing change.

K-018539.example: Typing 'alice' with 50ms gaps leaves validatorCalls at 0 at 250ms and at 1 at 350ms after the last keystroke. The debounce timer is 300ms, so the validator runs once and not five times.
K-018539.check: The debounce test prints 'All tests passed!' and expect(validatorCalls, 1) holds after the 300ms idle window.
traps: Using a real Timer or Future.delayed inside a test makes timing flaky, so stay inside fakeAsync.
Debouncing must not skip validation on submit, so test that submit still runs the validator at once.

steps.do: Create the test file for the quantity validator.
Write a test that runs the app with app.run_test(), types 0 into #qty with pilot.press, and asserts input.validate('0').is_valid is False.
Run the validation tests and expect every test to pass.
Run only the rejection tests to confirm they were collected and not skipped.

K-018540.example: A test types '0' into the #qty Input of a DataTable editor and asserts validate('0').is_valid is False. A second test types '5' and asserts is_valid is True.
K-018540.check: Pytest ends with '2 passed' and exit code 0, with no '1 skipped' line.
traps: Do not assert only on Input.value, because validation is separate from the stored text.
An async test without the asyncio marker can be skipped, so a green count may hide that nothing ran.
Always read the skipped count.

steps.do: Create the test file for the row-add guard.
Write a test that starts with a 3-row table, submits 'abc' into #qty, and presses enter.
Run the guard test and expect it to pass.
Run only the blocked-submit case to check that the row count stays at 3.

K-018541.example: The test submits 'abc' and asserts table.row_count is 3 before and after pressing enter. A valid submit of '4' is tested separately and asserts row_count becomes 4.
K-018541.check: Pytest prints '1 passed' for the blocked case, and the assertion message reports row_count == 3 after the invalid submit.
traps: Input.Changed fires on every keystroke, but Input.Submitted carries is_valid, so check event.is_valid before calling add_row.
A handler that adds rows on Changed will create rows while the user is still typing.

Write unit tests that call check_qty with '0', 'abc', and '5', and assert the exact Err message for the first two.

K-018544.check: Cargo prints 'test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed' for check_qty and exit code 0.

steps.do: List the input files that already exist in the project.
Read the Tailwind config to confirm the content paths that scan components.
Write down four states (idle, loading, error, success) and the class set for each.
Set the spinner show threshold to 200ms and the minimum display time to 300ms.
Confirm the plan lists exactly 4 states before moving to the build stage.

K-018545.example: The file src/components/SearchInput.tsx has an input whose disabled attribute is tied to isLoading, so the plan lists idle, loading with disabled:opacity-60, error with border-red-600, and success states. The spinner shows only after 200ms.
K-018545.check: rg -l prints src/components/SearchInput.tsx, and cat shows a content glob such as ./src/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}, which confirms the config scans the component.
traps: Small models plan only the loading state and skip error and success. Plan all 4 states.
Do not guess the Tailwind version; read it from the config or package.json.
Showing the spinner instantly causes flicker on fast responses, so the 200ms threshold is required.

steps.do: Confirm the installed Tailwind version, since the aria-busy variant needs version 3.2 or newer.
Set the disabled attribute on the input and aria-busy="true" on its wrapper while loading.
Choose the classes disabled:cursor-not-allowed, disabled:opacity-60, and aria-busy:cursor-progress.
Search for existing opacity classes on the same element to avoid a conflict.
Record a minimum contrast of 3:1 for the disabled input text against its background.

K-018546.example: The input in src/components/Field.tsx gets disabled plus disabled:opacity-60 and disabled:cursor-not-allowed, and its wrapper gets aria-busy:cursor-progress. The disabled text keeps a 3:1 contrast ratio against the background.
K-018546.check: npm ls tailwindcss prints a version of 3.2 or higher, which means the aria-busy variant exists.
traps: Small models assume aria-busy: works in Tailwind v2, but it needs v3.2 or newer.
Do not use readonly as a substitute for disabled while loading, because readonly inputs still look editable.
Do not stack two opacity utilities on one element.

steps.do: Find the height classes already used on inputs so the skeleton matches them.
Plan the skeleton as a div with animate-pulse, bg-gray-200, and rounded-md.
Set the skeleton height to h-10, which is 2.5rem or 40px, the same as the input.
Set aria-hidden="true" on the skeleton so screen readers skip it.
Confirm the skeleton and the input both use h-10 by searching the source.

K-018547.example: The input uses h-10, which is 40px, so the skeleton uses h-10 w-full animate-pulse rounded-md bg-gray-200 with aria-hidden="true".
K-018547.check: rg -n h-10 src lists both the input line and the skeleton line, each containing the class h-10.
traps: Small models pick a skeleton height that differs from the input, which causes layout shift.
Do not use animate-spin on a skeleton, since spin is for spinners and pulse is for placeholders.
Confirm bg-gray-200 exists in the default palette before naming it.

steps.do: Find spinner classes already used in the project.
Plan the spinner as animate-spin with motion-reduce:animate-none so rotation stops for users who prefer reduced motion.
Plan a visible text label Loading... beside the spinner so the state is still shown without motion.
Confirm the motion-reduce variant exists in the installed Tailwind version.
Set the spinner size to size-4, which is 1rem or 16px.

K-018548.example: The spinner in src/components/SearchInput.tsx uses size-4 animate-spin motion-reduce:animate-none, and a visible Loading... label sits beside it.
K-018548.check: rg -n motion-reduce src prints the spinner line, which confirms the variant is applied.
traps: Small models assume motion-reduce:animate-none hides the spinner, but it only stops the rotation.
Keep the text label, because a spinner that does not move gives no state signal on its own.
Do not write motion-safe:animate-spin without a reduced-motion fallback.

steps.do: Check existing padding-right classes so the spinner does not overlap typed text.
Plan the wrapper as relative and the spinner as absolute right-3 top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 size-4.
Set the input padding-right to pr-10, which is 2.5rem or 40px, to leave room for the 12px offset and the 16px spinner.
Set pointer-events-none on the spinner so clicks pass through to the input.
Confirm size-4 exists by checking that the installed Tailwind version is 3.4 or newer.

K-018549.example: The input gets pr-10 and the spinner gets pointer-events-none absolute right-3 top-1/2 size-4 -translate-y-1/2, so typed text stops 40px from the right edge.
K-018549.check: rg -n pr-10 src shows the input line, and npm ls tailwindcss prints 3.4.x or higher.
traps: Small models forget pointer-events-none, so the spinner blocks clicks on the input.
Center with top-1/2 and -translate-y-1/2, not top-0 alone.
The older w-4 h-4 pair works on any version, while size-4 needs Tailwind 3.4 or newer.

steps.do: Find existing delay and transition classes to avoid conflicts.
Plan the spinner wrapper with opacity-0, transition-opacity, delay-200, and duration-150.
Plan the switch to opacity-100 when the isLoading state is true.
Plan a minimum display time of 300ms so a fast response does not flicker.
Confirm the installed Tailwind version supports the delay-200 transition utility.

K-018550.example: The spinner wrapper has opacity-0 transition-opacity delay-200 duration-150, so a response under 200ms shows no spinner.
K-018550.check: rg -n delay-200 src prints the spinner line with the class, and npm ls tailwindcss prints the installed version.
traps: Small models treat delay-200 as an animation delay, but Tailwind's delay-* sets only the transition delay.
The timer must also change the JS state, because CSS alone does not know when the request ends.
Avoid durations under 150ms, which read as flicker.

steps.do: Confirm the tui session is already running. Start it by hand beforehand, and wait 200ms after the first render before typing.
Capture the pane before any input and confirm the form is drawn.
In the tui session, type the invalid quantity 'abc' and press Enter.
Capture the pane and confirm the error line is visible.
Kill the tui session so no stale process is left running.

K-018551.check: The capture-pane output contains the line 'Invalid quantity', and has-session -t tui exits non-zero after the kill.

Build minified CSS from the onboarding input file.
Measure the output size in bytes.

Add loading='lazy' and decoding='async' to each img below the first step, and add width and height attributes.
Wrap each image in a div with the Tailwind class aspect-video so space is reserved before it loads.
Run Lighthouse on the onboarding page and save the JSON report.

K-018553.check: The file lh-onboarding.json exists, and its cumulative-layout-shift audit numericValue is 0.1 or lower.

steps.do: Find transition-all and animation classes in the onboarding files.
Replace transition-all with transition-[transform,opacity] and prefix each animation class with motion-safe:.
Run the onboarding motion test that fails if width, height, or top animate.

K-018554.check: Playwright prints '1 passed', and the grep finds no transition-all lines in src/onboarding.

Leaving animations without motion-safe: ignores the user's reduced motion setting.

steps.do: Count lines with bracket pixel or rem values in each onboarding source file.
Replace each match with a spacing scale class, such as w-64 for 16rem.
Rebuild the onboarding CSS.
Print the final byte count of the built CSS.

K-018555.check: grep -rc prints 0 for every onboarding file, and wc -c shows fewer bytes than before the change.
traps: Swapping w-[256px] for a new arbitrary value adds a rule instead of removing one.
grep -c counts matching lines, not matches, so a line with two values counts once.

Read the Largest Contentful Paint value in milliseconds from the report.

steps.do: List every render function in the source tree.

Write one row per pane with columns pane, data source, empty state, and error state.

K-018568.example: rg finds render_list in src/ui.rs at line 42 and render_log at line 88, so the plan gets two rows. Each row names its data source and whether it needs an Empty state, an Error state, or both.
K-018568.check: wc -l docs/ui-states.md prints a number of at least 3, which is one header line plus one row per pane.
traps: Small models skip panes that only read config, but those can also fail.
Do not count render functions that only draw borders or titles.
Do not write render code during the plan stage.

steps.do: Count the toast token definitions in the light theme file.
List every var() reference to a toast token used by the component.
Type-check the component and its token typings.
Fail if any toast font-size is hardcoded in pixels instead of a token.

K-018569.example: light.css defines 6 --toast-* tokens, including --toast-title-size: 0.875rem, and Toast.tsx styles the title with var(--toast-title-size). The hardcoded-px grep prints nothing, so the component passes.
K-018569.check: The count prints 6, the var() list shows every defined token name, tsc exits 0 with no output, and the px grep prints nothing.
traps: A typo like --toast-titel-size still passes a simple count, so compare names exactly against the definitions.
Typed token maps accept any string, so tsc alone does not prove a token exists in the CSS.
A grep with no output means clean; do not read an empty result as a failure.

steps.do: Build the app so the toast demo route is current.
Create tests/toast-typography.spec.ts that opens /toast-demo, fires one success toast, and expects getComputedStyle font-size of [data-testid=toast-title] to be 14px.
Run only that spec with the line reporter.

K-018570.example: With a 16px root, --toast-title-size: 0.875rem resolves to 14px, so the spec expects the string 14px. A missing token falls back to 16px and fails with Received 16px.
K-018570.check: Output ends with 1 passed and no failed lines.
traps: Asserting the token string instead of the computed px value proves nothing about the rendered result.
Assuming a 16px root without checking it can give a wrong expected value when the app sets html font-size.
Running the spec before the build uses stale CSS and gives a false result.

steps.do: Start the dev server so the demo page is reachable on port 5173.
Run axe on the toast demo page limited to WCAG 2.1 AA rules and exit non-zero on violations.
Confirm normal text reaches 4.5:1 contrast and large text, meaning 24px regular or 18.66px bold, reaches 3:1.

K-018571.example: The warning variant sets --toast-warning-fg to #7a4b00 on #fff8e1, which must reach 4.5:1 for its 14px body text. axe reports a color-contrast violation with the selector .toast-warning if it falls below.
K-018571.check: axe exits 0 with no color-contrast entries for .toast-success, .toast-warning, or .toast-error.
traps: axe only audits the rendered state, so hover and focus colors need separate checks.
Running axe before the dev server starts tests nothing and may print a connection error.
Using the 3:1 large-text threshold for 14px body text passes a failing toast.

steps.do: Confirm the motion token is declared as 200ms in the light theme file.
Create tests/toast-motion.spec.ts that fires a toast and reads getComputedStyle transitionDuration on [data-testid=toast-root] expecting 0.2s.
Run the motion spec in the Chromium project only.
Check that the reduced-motion test reports 0s duration when prefers-reduced-motion is set.

K-018572.example: --toast-motion-enter: 200ms declared in light.css should compute to 0.2s on the toast root. Under reduced motion the spec expects 0s.
K-018572.check: The grep prints the declaration line with 200ms, and each Chromium run ends with 1 passed.
traps: getComputedStyle returns seconds such as 0.2s, not 200ms, so an exact ms string will never match.
Skipping the reduced-motion emulation misses a real accessibility regression.
A transition on a child element is not the root; read the duration from the element the token targets.

steps.do: Count toast token declarations in the light theme file.
Count toast token declarations in the dark theme file.
List the light theme token names so you can find any that are missing from dark.css.
Type-check the project, including the theme provider that switches data-theme on the html element.

K-018573.example: light.css and dark.css each declare 12 --toast-* tokens, including --toast-fg and --toast-bg. If dark.css shows 11 while light.css shows 12, one token is missing and the toast falls back to the light value in dark mode.
K-018573.check: Both counts print 12, the listed names all appear in dark.css, and tsc exits 0.
traps: Equal counts can still hide a renamed token, so compare the names from the list step, not just the totals.
Dark theme values may come from data-theme selectors on html, not from the file you counted.
A missing dark token will not error at build time, so the tsc pass does not prove parity.

steps.do: Find every font-family declaration in the Toast component folder.
Confirm no font-family value starts with anything other than the var() token; this should print nothing.
Lint the Toast folder with the project ESLint config and fail on any reported problem.
Run the spec that reads getComputedStyle fontFamily on the toast title and expects the token stack.

K-018574.example: Toast.module.css sets font-family: var(--toast-font-family), and light.css defines --toast-font-family as Inter, system-ui, sans-serif. The second grep finds no value outside that var() form, so it prints nothing.
K-018574.check: The first grep prints only var(--toast-font-family) lines, the second grep prints nothing, eslint reports 0 problems, and Playwright ends with 1 passed.
traps: A font-family set in a parent component can override the toast, so check the rendered computed value too.
Quoting the token name differently in the spec than in the CSS makes the comparison fail for the wrong reason.
An empty grep result means no raw values were found, so do not treat it as a tool error.

steps.do: Create the folder lib/widgets for the new widget file.
Create lib/widgets/adaptive_tabs.dart with a StatefulWidget that mixes in SingleTickerProviderStateMixin and creates a TabController in initState with length equal to the tab count.
In build, wrap the TabBar in a LayoutBuilder and set isScrollable to true when constraints.maxWidth is less than 600, otherwise false.
When isScrollable is true, set tabAlignment to TabAlignment.start so tabs align to the left edge.
Format the new file to the project style.
Run static analysis on the new file to catch unused imports and missing dispose calls.

K-018575.example: A TabBar with Home, Search, Saved, and Profile sets isScrollable to true at a maxWidth of 412 and to false at 900. The TabController is created once with length 4 in initState and disposed in dispose.
K-018575.check: flutter analyze prints 'No issues found!' and the TabBar reports isScrollable true at a width of 412 in a widget test.
traps: Creating the TabController inside build resets the selected tab on every rebuild, so create it once in initState.
Setting isScrollable without tabAlignment leaves tabs centered with uneven gaps, so set TabAlignment.start when scrolling.

steps.do: Create the test folder for widget tests.
Create test/widgets/adaptive_tabs_test.dart with a testWidgets case that sets tester.view.physicalSize to Size(320, 640) and tester.view.devicePixelRatio to 1.0.
In the same test, call addTearDown(tester.view.resetPhysicalSize) and pump the widget, then expect the TabBar isScrollable property to be true.
Add a second testWidgets case with physicalSize Size(800, 640) and expect isScrollable to be false.
Run the test file.

K-018576.example: At 320 by 640 with devicePixelRatio 1.0 the logical width is 320 and isScrollable is true. At 800 by 640 the logical width is 800 and isScrollable is false.
K-018576.check: flutter test prints 'All tests passed!' and reports 2 passing tests.
traps: Leaving devicePixelRatio at its default of 3.0 makes the logical width one third of the physical size, so the wrong breakpoint runs.
Skipping addTearDown(tester.view.resetPhysicalSize) leaks the surface size into later tests.

steps.do: Create the golden test folder under test/widgets.
Create test/widgets/adaptive_tabs_golden_test.dart that sets the surface to Size(360, 640) and calls expect(find.byType(AdaptiveTabs), matchesGoldenFile('goldens/tabs_360.png')).
Add a second golden case at Size(1200, 800) that calls matchesGoldenFile('goldens/tabs_1200.png').
Generate the baseline PNG files once.
Run the test again without the update flag to compare against the saved baselines.
List the saved baseline images to confirm both files exist.

K-018577.example: The test writes goldens/tabs_360.png and goldens/tabs_1200.png, and a later run fails with a diff image if the tab bar changes by one pixel.
K-018577.check: The second flutter test run prints 'All tests passed!' and ls lists tabs_1200.png and tabs_360.png.
traps: Generating goldens with a different font setup than CI produces diffs on every run, so generate them on the same platform used in CI.
Running with --update-goldens on every test run hides regressions by overwriting the baseline.

steps.do: Start the dev server on port 5173 for the test run.
Install the axe integration for Playwright as a dev dependency.
Write tests/empty-state-dark.spec.ts that sets colorScheme to dark, opens the empty route, and runs AxeBuilder withTags wcag2aa.
Run the dark-mode spec in chromium.
Confirm the axe results contain zero color-contrast violations for the empty state.

K-018578.example: The spec sets the heading color to #9aa3b2 on a #14161b background, a ratio of 6.9:1, which passes the 4.5:1 minimum for normal text. A later edit that lowers the text to #4b5263 gives about 2.4:1, and axe then reports a color-contrast node.
K-018578.check: Playwright prints 1 passed, and the axe violations array has length 0 for color-contrast.
traps: Small models test only the light theme and miss dark-mode failures.
Axe skips elements that are hidden when the scan runs, so the empty state must be rendered first.
A successful build does not prove contrast.

steps.do: Create the tests folder if it does not exist.
Write tests/empty-theme.spec.ts that calls page.emulateMedia with colorScheme dark, then reads getComputedStyle of .empty-state for background-color.
Run the theme spec in chromium.
Confirm the computed background is rgb(20, 22, 27) in dark mode and rgb(248, 249, 251) in light mode.

K-018579.example: The light token --empty-bg is #f8f9fb and the dark token is #14161b, and the spec expects rgb(20, 22, 27) after emulating dark. If the spec still reads rgb(248, 249, 251), the dark block in app.css is missing or overridden.
K-018579.check: Playwright reports 2 passed (one per scheme), and both computed background values match the stated rgb numbers.
traps: Small models check only the default light value and assume dark works.
The dark rule must sit inside a prefers-color-scheme dark media query or a data-theme selector, not after a light override with the same specificity.

steps.do: Confirm the inline theme script sits in src/app.html before the sveltekit head placeholder.
Write tests/theme-persist.spec.ts that sets localStorage theme to dark, reloads, and checks the html data-theme attribute within 200ms of DOMContentLoaded.
Run the persistence spec in chromium.

K-018580.example: The app.html script reads localStorage.theme and sets document.documentElement.dataset.theme to dark before the head placeholder. The spec measures the attribute at 42ms after DOMContentLoaded, which is under the 200ms limit.
K-018580.check: rg prints the data-theme line above the %sveltekit.head% line, and Playwright reports 1 passed.
traps: Small models put the theme script after the Svelte bundle, which causes a flash on reload.
Do not treat a passing test on first load as proof, because only the reload path shows the flash.

steps.do: Start the dev server on port 5173 if it is not already running.
Run Lighthouse with only the accessibility category and save the JSON report.
Read the accessibility score from the report.
Confirm the button CSS sets min-height to 44px.

K-018581.example: The Lighthouse score prints 1 for a passing page, and the action button has min-height: 44px at line 38 of EmptyState.svelte. A score of 0.87 would mean at least one contrast or label issue remains.
K-018581.check: jq prints 1, and rg prints one match containing min-height: 44px.
traps: Small models accept a score of 0.9 as passing, but this card needs exactly 1.
Lighthouse runs one theme only, so run it once in dark mode by setting colorScheme in the page before the audit.

steps.do: Create lib/widgets/tabs_shell.dart with a LayoutBuilder that returns a Row when maxWidth is at least 840 and a Column with TabBar on top otherwise.
In the expanded branch, place a NavigationRail with destinations equal to the tab count and labelType set to NavigationRailLabelType.all on the left of an Expanded TabBarView.
Connect NavigationRail onDestinationSelected to TabController.animateTo so both controls share one index.
Check the file with static analysis.

K-018582.example: At a maxWidth of 1024 the shell shows a NavigationRail with 3 destinations on the left, and at 500 it shows a TabBar with 3 tabs above the view. Both controls use one TabController of length 3.
K-018582.check: flutter analyze prints 'No issues found!' and the NavigationRail destination count equals the TabBar tab count in the test.
traps: Building two separate TabControllers lets the rail and the bar show different selected tabs after a resize.
NavigationRail with fewer than 2 destinations fails an assertion at runtime, so guard the tab count.

steps.do: Create test/widgets/adaptive_tabs_resize_test.dart with a testWidgets case that pumps AdaptiveTabs at physicalSize Size(360, 640) and devicePixelRatio 1.0.
In the same test, tap the third Tab and then change tester.view.physicalSize to Size(1200, 800) and call pumpAndSettle.
Expect find.byType(Tab) to find exactly 4 widgets after the resize.
Expect the third tab to still be selected by checking TabBar controller index equals 2.
Run the resize test file.

K-018583.example: After tapping the tab at index 2 and resizing from 360 to 1200 wide, the tab count is 4 and the controller index is 2.
K-018583.check: flutter test prints 'All tests passed!' and the resize test reports 1 passing test.
traps: Recreating the TabController on breakpoint change drops the selected index to 0.
Changing the surface size without calling pumpAndSettle checks the old layout and reports a false pass.

steps.do: Create test/widgets/adaptive_tabs_text_scale_test.dart with a testWidgets case that wraps AdaptiveTabs in MediaQuery with textScaler set to TextScaler.linear(2.0).
In the same test, set tester.view.physicalSize to Size(360, 640) and devicePixelRatio to 1.0 before pumping.
Expect tester.getSize of the first Tab widget to have height greaterThanOrEqualTo 48.0.
Expect the TabBar height to be at least 48.0 and check that no RenderFlex overflow error is reported.
Run the text scale test file.

K-018584.example: At textScaler 2.0 on a 360 by 640 surface, the first Tab measures 56.0 tall, which is at least 48.0, and the test passes.
K-018584.check: flutter test prints 'All tests passed!' with no 'A RenderFlex overflowed' message in the output.
traps: Passing textScaleFactor, which is deprecated, instead of textScaler does not apply the scale in current Flutter versions.
A tab height below 48.0 fails the touch target rule, so set a minimum height on the Tab rather than shrinking the font.

steps.do: Run svelte-check across the project and stop on errors only.
Run svelte-check with machine output and confirm the summary line reports 0 ERRORS.
If errors appear, locate the theme prop declaration in the component.
Open the file named in the first error, change the $props type for theme to a union of the allowed names, then rerun the check and confirm 0 ERRORS.

K-018585.example: A prop declared as theme: 'light' | 'dark' in $props() gets checked, and passing theme='blue' on the page shows an error at that line. After the fix the summary prints 0 ERRORS and 0 WARNINGS.
K-018585.check: The machine output summary reads 0 ERRORS and the run exits with code 0.
traps: Small models rely on the dev server running without errors and skip the type check.
A prop typed as string instead of a union lets bad theme names pass silently.

steps.do: Start the dev server so the menu page is served on localhost port 3000.
Run the Playwright spec that sets viewports to 767px and 768px and checks menu visibility.
Confirm the spec asserts that the toggle button is visible at 767px and hidden at 768px.
Count the md-prefixed classes in the menu component to confirm the desktop nav uses md:flex and the toggle uses md:hidden.

K-018586.example: At 767px the button with aria-label="Open menu" is visible and the nav list has class "hidden md:flex", so the list stays hidden. At 768px the button is hidden and the nav list is displayed as flex.
K-018586.check: Playwright prints a line like "2 passed" with no "failed" lines, and grep prints a count of at least 2.
traps: Tailwind is mobile-first, so unprefixed classes apply at every width; a small model often forgets the base class or writes max-md: by mistake.
Testing only one width such as 375px misses the switch at 768px.
Putting md:hidden on a wrapper can hide both the toggle and the nav, so check each element separately.

steps.do: Build the Tailwind stylesheet from the input file into dist/out.css.
Count the 768px min-width media query blocks in the compiled CSS.
Confirm the compiled CSS contains the escaped md:hidden selector.

K-018587.example: After the build, dist/out.css contains one @media (width >= 48rem) block with .md\:hidden and .md\:flex rules. The grep for md:hidden returns 1.
K-018587.check: The build exits with a line such as "Done in 120ms", and grep prints counts of at least 1 for both checks.
traps: md is 48rem (768px) in Tailwind, not 768px in the CSS source; grep for the rem form.
If the menu class is not in any scanned file, Tailwind drops the rule silently, so the count is 0 with no error.
Using the v3 command npx tailwindcss against a v4 project produces a wrong or failed build.

steps.do: Run Lighthouse in mobile form factor on the menu page and write the JSON report.
Print the accessibility category score from the report.
Compare the printed score with the required threshold of 0.9.

K-018588.example: The mobile run on localhost:3000 writes a report whose accessibility score is 0.96. The threshold is 0.9, so the menu passes.
K-018588.check: The node command prints a number between 0 and 1, and the value is 0.9 or higher.
traps: Lighthouse scores are 0 to 1 in the JSON, not 0 to 100, so 96 is never the value.
The dev server must be running first, or Lighthouse reports a connection error and writes no score.
A high score does not prove the menu works at 320px, so pair it with a viewport test.

steps.do: Run the Playwright spec that loads the menu at 375px and reads each button and link bounding box.
Count the menu links in the component that have the py-3 or h-11 classes, which give at least 44px height.
Confirm the spec asserts height of 44 or more for each target.

K-018589.example: At 375px each mobile link has class py-3 with text-base, so its box is 48px tall. The spec asserts boundingBox().height >= 44 for all six links and passes.
K-018589.check: Playwright prints "passed" with no failures, and the spec's assertion lists 44 as the minimum height.
traps: Tailwind h-11 is 2.75rem, which is 44px only when the root font size is 16px; a small model should check the computed value.
Padding alone does not count if the link is inline; add block or flex display first.
Icon-only buttons often measure 24px, which fails the 44px target.

steps.do: Run the Playwright spec that sets the viewport to 320px wide and compares page scroll width.
Confirm the spec evaluates document.documentElement.scrollWidth and asserts it is at most 320.
Count the whitespace-nowrap and w-screen classes in the menu, since these often cause overflow.

K-018590.example: At 320px the page scrollWidth is 320, so no sideways scroll occurs. The grep finds one w-screen class in the mobile panel, which the spec shows is safe because the panel has max-w-full.
K-018590.check: Playwright reports the overflow test as passed, and the scrollWidth assertion equals or is below 320.
traps: Using w-screen on a nested element can exceed the parent width, so check the scrollWidth value rather than trusting the class.
Testing at 375px alone misses overflow that only appears at 320px.
A scrollWidth check does not catch hidden overflow with overflow-hidden, so also confirm the menu items are visible.

steps.do: Run the Playwright spec that clicks the toggle at 375px and reads aria-expanded before and after the click.
Run the axe accessibility check on the menu page at 375px width.
Confirm the spec asserts aria-expanded equals "false" before the click and "true" after.

K-018591.example: At 375px the button starts with aria-expanded="false", and after one click the panel shows and the attribute is "true". The axe run reports 0 violations.
K-018591.check: Playwright reports the aria test as passed, and axe reports 0 violations for the menu page.
traps: aria-expanded must be the string "true" or "false", not a boolean in the HTML attribute.
Tailwind hidden classes remove the panel from the accessibility tree, so the panel must be shown before checking its links.
Hiding the toggle at md with md:hidden also removes its aria-expanded from view, so check the attribute only at widths where the toggle exists.

steps.do: Find size or padding settings in menu files that could shrink the tap area.
Record that kMinInteractiveDimension is 48.0 in package:flutter/material.dart and use it as the floor.
Write a plan line that every menu item has a minimum width and height of 48.0 logical pixels.
Name the test file the build stage must make pass, using androidTapTargetGuideline.

K-018592.example: A MenuItemButton with style minimumSize of Size(32, 32) fails the floor, so the plan changes it to Size(48, 48). The test file is test/a11y/menu_tap_target_test.dart.
K-018592.check: rg prints no minimumSize smaller than 48 in the menu files, and the planned test prints All tests passed! once built.
traps: Do not measure the visible icon size as the tap target; the padded hit area is what counts.
If the plan also covers iOS, state the 44.0 guideline separately so the two are not mixed.

steps.do: Find icon-only triggers by searching for IconButton and PopupMenuButton.
Find which triggers already set a tooltip, since tooltip becomes the screen reader label.
Decide that every icon-only trigger gets a tooltip string or a Semantics label describing its action.
Name the test the build stage must pass, which checks labels with labeledTapTargetGuideline.

K-018593.example: The overflow button in lib/ui/toolbar.dart uses Icons.more_vert with no tooltip, so the plan adds tooltip: 'More options'. The count of unlabeled triggers goes from 1 to 0.
K-018593.check: The tooltip search lists a line for each icon-only trigger, and the planned test prints All tests passed! once built.
traps: A tooltip on a parent does not label a child that is excluded from semantics.
Do not use labels like 'button' or 'icon', which name the control type instead of its action.

steps.do: Find existing Shortcuts, Actions, and CallbackShortcuts widgets so the plan reuses them.
Find FocusNode and Focus uses, since a menu without them cannot receive keyboard focus.
Decide that Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger, bound with SingleActivator(LogicalKeyboardKey.escape).
Decide that arrow keys move between MenuItemButton entries, which MenuAnchor handles natively.
Name the widget test the build stage must pass, which sends an Escape key event.

K-018594.example: A MenuBar in lib/ui/app_bar.dart needs Escape to close, so the plan wraps it in CallbackShortcuts with SingleActivator(LogicalKeyboardKey.escape). The test sends the key with tester.sendKeyEvent and expects the MenuController isOpen value to be false.
K-018594.check: rg shows a CallbackShortcuts or Shortcuts line near each MenuBar, and the planned test prints All tests passed! once built.
traps: Do not assume Escape works on a PopupMenuButton without a test that proves it.
The plan must say where focus goes after close, which is back to the trigger.

steps.do: Find hard-coded colors in menu files that bypass the theme.
Find menu styles that set foregroundColor or a text style color directly.
Record each text and background pair from ColorScheme, such as onSurface on surface.
Require at least 4.5 to 1 for body text and at least 3 to 1 for text 18pt or larger, and mark disabled items as exempt.
Name the test the build stage must pass, which uses textContrastGuideline on the menu.

K-018595.example: A custom item in lib/ui/menu_theme.dart uses Color(0xFF9E9E9E) on Color(0xFFFFFFFF), a ratio of about 2.7 to 1, so the plan switches the text to ColorScheme.onSurface. The new pair must measure at least 4.5 to 1.
K-018595.check: rg finds no hard-coded grey below 4.5 to 1 on the menu surface, and the planned test prints All tests passed! once built.
traps: Judge contrast by computing the ratio from relative luminance, not by how the colors look.
Disabled items are exempt from WCAG, but the plan should still list which items are disabled.

steps.do: Find fixed heights on menu items, since they clip scaled text.
Find textScaleFactor and textScaler uses, since textScaleFactor is deprecated.
Plan a test that wraps the menu in MediaQuery with textScaler set to TextScaler.linear(2.0).
Plan to replace fixed heights with ConstrainedBox minHeight constraints so labels can grow.
Name the golden test the build stage must pass at 2.0 scale.

K-018596.example: A MenuItemButton in lib/ui/menu.dart wraps its Text in SizedBox(height: 40), so at 2.0 scale the label is cut off. The plan changes it to ConstrainedBox(constraints: BoxConstraints(minHeight: 48)), and the 2.0 golden must show the full label.
K-018596.check: rg shows no fixed height on menu items, and the golden comparison at 2.0 scale reports zero differing pixels once the build stage is done.
traps: Testing only at scale 1.0 hides clipping, so the plan must include the 2.0 case.
Overflow appears as a RenderFlex overflow message in test output, so the verify step must search for it.

steps.do: Confirm the app file exists in the project root.
Confirm Textual is installed in the active Python environment.
Add a test that runs the app with run_test(size=(40, 20)) and another with size=(80, 24).
Run the responsive test file at both sizes.
Check that the #email Input width is 38 at 40 columns and 60 at 80 columns, and that the form container layout is vertical at 40 columns.

K-018597.example: At size (40, 20) the test reads #email region.width == 38 and asserts the narrow class is set on the form screen. At size (80, 24) the same Input must report region.width == 60 because form_app.tcss sets max-width: 60.
K-018597.check: pytest prints '2 passed' and exits with status 0; any width mismatch prints an AssertionError with the actual value.
traps: Textual has no @media queries, so read self.size in on_resize or check the size in the test instead.
Testing only at the default 80x24 hides narrow-width failures.
Do not run a real terminal to check; use app.run_test(size=...).

steps.do: Confirm Cargo.toml lists the ratatui dependency.
Run the form layout tests.
Check that src/form_layout.rs matches rustfmt style without changing it.
In the test, create TestBackend::new(40, 12) and assert the first Input rect width is 40 with a single column.
Run the full test suite to confirm no other test broke.

K-018598.example: A test builds Terminal::new(TestBackend::new(40, 12)) and asserts Layout::horizontal produces 1 column with the first Input width 40. A second test uses TestBackend::new(100, 12) and asserts 2 columns with the first width 50.
K-018598.check: cargo test prints 'test result: ok' with 2 passed, and rustfmt --check exits with status 0 and no output.
traps: Do not run the crossterm event loop in tests, because it blocks; use ratatui::backend::TestBackend.
Read the rendered cells with terminal.backend().buffer(), not stdout.
Use real names like Layout::horizontal and Constraint::Percentage, not an invented breakpoint API.

steps.do: List every line under lib that mentions a Flutter menu widget.
steps.cmd: rg -n -e MenuAnchor -e MenuBar -e PopupMenuButton -e SubmenuButton -e MenuItemButton lib

steps.do: Count the menu widget matches so the plan has a fixed total.
steps.cmd: rg -c -e MenuAnchor -e MenuBar -e PopupMenuButton -e SubmenuButton -e MenuItemButton lib

steps.do: Read the Flutter version number in the output and confirm it is 3.7.0 or higher, because MenuAnchor requires it.
Run the analyzer and confirm it reports 0 issues before you trust the inventory.
Write the inventory as a table with file, line, widget name, and whether the trigger has a label.
Check that the table has one row for each match counted in step 2.

K-018599.example: The search finds 4 matches across lib/ui/nav_menu.dart and lib/ui/editor_toolbar.dart, so the plan table gets 4 rows. The version check reads 3.22.0, and flutter analyze reports 0 issues. Each row records the widget, the file line, and yes or no for a label.
K-018599.check: flutter analyze reports 0 issues, and the table has the same number of rows as the total printed by rg -c in step 2, for example 4.
traps: Searching only for MenuAnchor misses PopupMenuButton, which is older and still common.
Do not count matches in test/ as app menus unless the plan covers tests.
A Flutter version below 3.7.0 means MenuAnchor will not compile, so stop and report that before planning.

steps.do: Confirm the formcheck session exists.
Capture the pane and read the output.
If the capture is blank, capture again, because the first frame may not be drawn yet.
Count the printed lines in the capture. The count must be exactly 12.
