Reading an old dist file without rebuilding shows stale results.
Expecting the md breakpoint at 640px; Tailwind's md starts at 768px and sm starts at 640px.

steps.do: Create the overflow spec file.
Write a test that sets the viewport to 320x568 and asserts document.documentElement.scrollWidth equals 320.
Run the overflow spec on Chromium.
Search the components for fixed pixel widths that can overflow small screens.
Replace any fixed width with w-full max-w-md and re-run the spec.

K-018666.example: An input with class w-[400px] makes scrollWidth 400 at a 320px viewport, which fails. Changing it to w-full max-w-md makes scrollWidth 320, which passes.
K-018666.check: The spec prints '1 passed', and the failing run prints scrollWidth 400 against expected 320.
traps: Using w-[400px] or other arbitrary fixed widths on inputs causes overflow on phones.
Checking scrollWidth on the body instead of the document element can hide overflow.
Setting the viewport to 375px and assuming 320px passes too; narrower screens need their own test.

steps.do: Build the app so Tailwind generates the animate-spin utility.
Run the Playwright spec that delays the options request and checks the spinner.
Confirm the spec asserts the spinner element has the animate-spin class.
Confirm the built CSS contains the animate-spin utility.
Confirm the spinner sits inside the select wrapper so it stays in the accessibility tree.

K-018667.example: The spec delays the /api/colors route by 800ms, then checks that the element with data-testid spinner has the class animate-spin and is visible. After the response it checks that the spinner is hidden within 1000ms.
K-018667.check: Playwright prints 1 passed, and rg prints a count of 1 or more for animate-spin.
traps: Small models often build the class name dynamically, such as animate-${x}, which Tailwind purges at build time. Write each class as a full literal string in the source.
Do not wait a fixed number of milliseconds; wait for the spinner with an expect assertion. Keep the spinner inside the select wrapper so it stays in the accessibility tree.

steps.do: Build the app so Tailwind generates the disabled variant classes.
Run the axe accessibility scan on the signup page with the loading state forced on.
Run the Playwright spec that checks the select has the disabled attribute and aria-busy set to true.
Confirm the select source uses the disabled utility classes for opacity and cursor.
Confirm the select text keeps at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background.

K-018668.example: The select renders with disabled and aria-busy=true, and the classes disabled:cursor-not-allowed and disabled:opacity-60 are applied. The axe scan reports zero violations for the select, and the label text keeps a 4.5:1 contrast ratio.
K-018668.check: axe reports zero violations, the Playwright spec prints 1 passed, and grep prints one matching line in Select.tsx.
traps: Small models set disabled without aria-busy, so screen readers announce nothing about loading. Set both attributes together.
Lowering opacity alone can drop text contrast below 4.5:1. Keep the text color dark enough and check the ratio.

steps.do: Build the app so the preview server serves the production bundle.
Start the production preview server on port 4173.
Run the Lighthouse accessibility audit on the signup page and save the report as JSON.
Print the accessibility score from the report.
Compare the printed score against the 0.9 gate and record the result.

K-018669.example: The signup page with a loading select is audited on the preview build, and the accessibility score comes back as 0.96. The jq output of 0.96 is above the 0.9 gate, so the page passes.
K-018669.check: jq prints a number of 0.9 or higher, such as 0.96; any value under 0.9 fails the gate.
traps: Small models read the score as a percentage out of 100 and misjudge the 0.9 threshold. The score is a fraction between 0 and 1.
Do not run Lighthouse against the dev server with hot reload. Use the production preview build, and do not treat a passing score as proof that the spinner works.

steps.do: Run the Playwright spec that aborts the options request with a network failure.
Confirm the spec asserts an element with role alert shows the error text.
Typecheck the select props so the loading and error fields are declared.
Confirm the error message uses the text-red-700 class, which has more than 4.5:1 contrast on white.
Confirm the spinner is removed in a finally block, not only on success.

K-018670.example: The spec routes /api/colors to abort, waits up to 3000ms, and expects the spinner to be gone and an element with role alert to show Could not load options. The grep finds text-red-700 on a white background, which is above the 4.5:1 contrast minimum.
K-018670.check: Playwright prints 1 passed, tsc exits with no output, and grep prints the matching line from Select.tsx.
traps: Small models clear the loading flag only on success, so a failed fetch leaves the select locked forever. Clear it in a finally block.
Do not show the error with color alone. Add visible text and role alert so the failure is announced.

steps.do: Run the unit tests filtered to the select loading hook.
Confirm the test advances timers by exactly 200ms before checking the flag.
Run the type checker to confirm the hook return type includes an isLoading boolean.
Count the test cases in the loading test file to confirm at least 3 exist.
Confirm the assertion checks that the spinner class is gone after the timers advance.

K-018671.example: The test sets isLoading to true, resolves the fetch, then calls vi.advanceTimersByTime(200) and expects the spinner to be gone. The grep shows the advanceTimersByTime(200) line, and rg counts 4 matching test lines.
K-018671.check: npm test reports all tests passing, grep shows the advanceTimersByTime(200) line, and rg prints a count of 3 or more.
traps: Small models assert that the spinner is removed immediately, which fails when React batches updates. Advance fake timers or use waitFor.
Do not hardcode a real 200ms sleep in the test. Confirm the type check covers the hook file as well.

steps.do: Run the Playwright spec that measures the select box height before and during loading.
Confirm the select wrapper uses the fixed height class h-10 in the source.
Run Lighthouse on the preview build and save the performance report as JSON.
Print the cumulative layout shift value from the report.
Confirm the printed layout shift value is 0.1 or less.

K-018672.example: The spec records the select box height as 40px before loading and 40px during loading, a difference of 0px. The jq output of 0.02 is under the 0.1 layout shift limit.
K-018672.check: Playwright reports 1 passed, and jq prints a number at most 0.1.
traps: Small models swap the label for a taller spinner, so the box grows. Keep h-10 on both the loading and loaded states.
Do not treat a dev build's layout shift as final. Measure on the preview build and compare heights in px.

steps.do: Create the spec file for input width checks.
Edit the file to add tests that set the viewport to 320x568 and 768x1024, then assert the input boundingBox width equals the container's content width.
Edit playwright.config.ts so webServer runs 'npm run dev -- --port 5173' at http://localhost:5173. Playwright starts the server itself.
Run the width spec with Playwright.
Confirm the run reports two passed tests and zero failed.

K-018673.example: At 320px, a container with p-4 has 288px of content width, so an input with class w-full border px-3 must measure 288px. At 768px, the same input inside a max-w-md mx-auto wrapper must measure 448px.
K-018673.check: Playwright prints '2 passed' with no 'failed' line; a failure shows expected and received widths for the viewport that broke.
traps: Testing only one viewport misses the phone case, where padding shrinks the box.
Hard-coding 288 without reading the container padding breaks when the spacing class changes.
Running the spec before the dev server is up gives connection errors, not width results. The webServer entry in playwright.config.ts avoids this.

steps.do: Create the tap target spec file.
Edit the file to set the viewport to 375x812 and assert the input boundingBox height is at least 44. Confirm playwright.config.ts webServer runs 'npm run dev -- --port 5173'.
Run the tap target spec.
If it fails, find the height class on the input component.
Change the height class to h-11 (2.75rem, 44px), then re-run the spec and confirm it passes.

K-018674.example: An input with class h-11 w-full rounded-md border px-3 text-base measures 44px tall at 375px wide. The earlier h-10 class measured 40px and failed the 44px minimum.
K-018674.check: The spec prints '1 passed', and the failing run prints an assertion showing height 40 against expected at least 44.
traps: h-10 is 40px, which fails; a small model often assumes it is close enough.
Using py-2 with text-sm can leave the input under 44px even when the text looks normal.
Checking only at desktop width misses the mobile sizes where the target matters.

steps.do: Build the production bundle.
Edit playwright.config.ts so webServer runs 'npm run preview -- --port 4173' at http://localhost:4173. Playwright starts the preview server itself.
Create the mobile accessibility spec file.
Edit the file to set the viewport to 375x812, open /signup, and run @axe-core/playwright with the wcag2aa tags, asserting zero violations.
Run the mobile accessibility spec and confirm it reports one passed test.

K-018675.example: A placeholder with text-gray-500 (#6b7280) on a white background has a contrast ratio of 4.83:1, which passes the 4.5:1 AA threshold. A text-gray-400 placeholder (#9ca3af) is about 2.5:1 and fails.
K-018675.check: The Playwright spec prints '1 passed'; a failing run lists each axe violation with its rule id and the count of violations.
traps: Passing an input without a visible label because the placeholder is present; placeholders are not labels.
Checking contrast only at desktop width misses mobile layout changes that move text onto a different background.
Reading only the last line of output can hide violations; check the full list of axe results.

steps.do: Search the toast source for the broad transition-all class, which animates every property.
Confirm the transition classes name only transform or opacity.
Count the duration-200 classes, which set the 200ms time for enter and exit.
Run the Playwright spec that checks animated properties at runtime.

K-018676.example: The toast uses transition-transform and transition-opacity classes, and the transition-all search returns no lines. The duration-200 count should be 2, one for enter and one for exit.
K-018676.check: The transition-all search prints nothing and exits with 1; the count prints 2; Playwright prints '1 passed'.
traps: A pattern with parentheses or pipes breaks in bash unless it is quoted.
transition-all is not an error but animates layout properties, so it must have zero matches.
A passing spec does not prove the property list, so read the rg output too.

steps.do: Show the content globs in the Tailwind config to confirm they include the toast folder.
Search for dynamic class names built with string interpolation, which Tailwind cannot detect.
Build the minified CSS from the input file.
Measure the size of the built CSS in bytes.
Confirm a toast slide class survived the build.

K-018677.example: The config lists './src/**/*.{ts,tsx}' as content, and the interpolation search returns nothing. The built app.css is 14302 bytes and contains translate-x-full at least once.
K-018677.check: The content glob includes src/components; the interpolation search prints nothing; stat prints a number under 20000; the rg count prints 1 or more.
traps: Class names built from template strings such as bg-${color} are purged from the build and never appear.
Without --minify the size check is meaningless because the output is much larger.
Tailwind only generates classes it finds as complete literal strings in the content files.

steps.do: Search the toast container for the pointer-events classes.
Count fixed positioning classes on the container, which should be exactly 1.
Run the Playwright hit-test spec that clicks a button under the toast area.

K-018678.example: The container has pointer-events-none and each toast item has pointer-events-auto. The fixed count is 1 and the hit-test spec clicks a button behind the container successfully.
K-018678.check: The pointer-events search shows pointer-events-none on the container and pointer-events-auto on the item; Playwright prints '1 passed'.
traps: Setting pointer-events-none on the toast items too makes the close button unclickable.
A fixed container with no pointer-events class blocks clicks on everything beneath it.
Check the item class names exactly, since pointer-events-auto is a Tailwind class and not a CSS rule you write.

steps.do: Create a reports directory to hold the Lighthouse output.
Run Lighthouse on the toast demo page in headless Chrome, limited to the performance category.
Read the performance score from the report, which must be 0.9 or higher.
Read the cumulative layout shift value, which must be under 0.1.

K-018679.example: The demo runs on localhost port 3000 and the report is written to reports/toast.json. The score prints 0.94 and the layout shift prints 0.02.
K-018679.check: jq prints a score of 0.9 or higher and a layout shift under 0.1; the dev server must already be running on port 3000.
traps: Lighthouse against a dev server with hot reload gives noisy numbers, so use a production build when comparing results.
A missing dev server makes Lighthouse fail with a connection error, not a low score.
Read the numeric value field, not the displayValue text, when comparing against thresholds.

steps.do: Count setTimeout calls in the toast source.
Count clearTimeout calls in the toast source, which must match the setTimeout count.
Run the Playwright spec that adds five toasts and checks that only three are visible.

K-018680.example: The source has 2 setTimeout calls and 2 clearTimeout calls, one pair for auto-dismiss and one for the exit animation. The cap spec adds five toasts and sees three.
K-018680.check: Both counts print 2; Playwright prints '1 passed' with the visible count assertion of 3.
traps: Counting calls in test files instead of the component gives a false match.
A cap of three means extra toasts are queued or dropped, not rendered and hidden with CSS.
Timers without cleanup on unmount keep running after the toast is removed.

steps.do: Type-check the project without emitting files.
Build the production bundle with Vite.
Measure the size in bytes of the toast chunk in the build output.
Run the Playwright timing spec that measures time from trigger click to toast visible.

K-018681.example: The type check passes and the build writes dist/assets/toast.js at 3120 bytes. The timing spec measures 143ms from click to visible toast.
K-018681.check: tsc prints no errors; stat prints a number under 4096; Playwright prints '1 passed' with the measured time under 200ms.
traps: The chunk file name changes with a hash, so check the name in the build output before measuring.
A passing timing test on a fast machine does not prove the budget holds on slower hardware.
tsc errors do not stop Vite from building, so read the tsc output separately.

steps.do: Create the store module named index.svelte.ts so runes work outside components.
Declare the current locale with $state and type it as 'en' or 'de' or 'ar'.
Derive the active dictionary with $derived from the current locale.
Export the state through an object with a getter so importers see updates.
Type-check the new module.

K-018682.example: The store starts with locale 'en', and t('menu.open') returns 'Open menu'. After setting locale to 'ar', the derived dictionary switches and t returns the Arabic string.
K-018682.check: npx tsc --noEmit exits with code 0 and prints no errors.
traps: A file without the .svelte.ts suffix will not compile runes, so the name matters.
Exporting a reassigned let variable loses reactivity for importers; use a getter object instead.

steps.do: Build the option list from the locale codes array in the store, not from typed labels.
Create each native name with new Intl.DisplayNames using type language and the code.
Bind the select element with bind:value to the store locale.
Print the native name for Arabic to confirm the output.
Run the switcher unit tests.

K-018683.example: The select offers English, Deutsch and the Arabic native name. The node command prints the Arabic word for Arabic.
K-018683.check: node prints the Arabic script word for Arabic, and vitest reports all tests passed.
traps: Typed language labels drift from the locale list, so always derive them from the codes.
Do not forget to update the document lang attribute when the select changes.

steps.do: Add a keydown handler on the element with role menu that handles ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End.
When dir is rtl, make ArrowLeft move to the next item and ArrowRight to the previous item.
Set tabindex to -1 on all items except the active one, and move focus with element.focus.
Create the Playwright spec file for the right-to-left keyboard test.
Run the right-to-left keyboard test against the built app.

K-018684.example: On the Arabic locale, pressing ArrowLeft focuses the next item and ArrowRight focuses the previous one. The spec then checks both moves.
K-018684.check: The Playwright output reports 1 passed or more and 0 failed.
traps: In RTL, ArrowLeft means previous only in the horizontal case, so mapping it the same as LTR is a common error.
Leaving tabindex at 0 on every item makes Tab skip through the whole menu.

steps.do: Create the root layout file.
Import the locale store and add an $effect that sets document.documentElement.lang to the current locale.
In that same $effect, set document.documentElement.dir to rtl for ar and ltr for other locales, on a separate line.
Count the lines that write to documentElement, which must be 2.
Type-check the Svelte project with a strict error threshold.

K-018685.example: After switching to ar, the html element has lang set to ar and dir set to rtl. The grep count of documentElement lines is 2.
K-018685.check: grep -c prints 2 and svelte-check reports 0 errors.
traps: Write dir to documentElement, not to body, so the whole page direction is set.
Use $effect for DOM writes, since it runs only in the browser and not during server rendering.

steps.do: Confirm the input references the error element id in its markup.
Run the TextField unit tests that cover the error state.
Confirm the error paragraph has role alert so screen readers announce it.

K-018686.example: TextField.tsx sets aria-describedby to errorId only when error is set, and the error p element has id errorId and role alert. The vitest case renders error='Enter a valid email' and expects that text in the DOM with the input's accessible description.
K-018686.check: grep prints a line such as 22: aria-describedby={error ? errorId : undefined}, and vitest prints Tests 3 passed (3) with exit code 0.
traps: A static id such as error repeats when two fields show errors, so the link points to the wrong field.
Leaving role alert off means no announcement, even when the text is visible.
Unit tests do not prove the link works in a browser, so run the Playwright check too.

steps.do: Read the spec to confirm it targets the signup email field.
Run the error-state spec with the line reporter.
Confirm the spec asserts the error appears within 200ms of blur.

K-018687.example: The spec types bad@ into the email field, blurs it, and expects the role alert text Enter a valid email to be visible within 200ms. It then types a valid address and expects that text to be hidden.
K-018687.check: Playwright prints 1 passed with exit code 0, and grep prints a line containing timeout: 200.
traps: A test that waits for a fixed sleep hides a slow error state, so use an explicit timeout.
Checking only the text without checking that it clears misses stale errors.
Blur is required for most inline validation, so a test that only types will not trigger the error.

steps.do: Scan the empty-state signup page with axe.
Scan the error-state page that the dev fixture renders with error=1.
Confirm the error fixture route is wired in the dev server.

K-018688.example: Both axe runs use the local dev server on port 5173, and the error page shows the email field in its invalid state with the message below it. The scan reports no violations for either URL.
K-018688.check: Both axe commands exit with status 0, and any violation makes the command exit with status 1.
traps: Scanning only the empty page misses errors that appear after submit.
A fixture that does not render the error state makes the scan pass without testing anything.
axe finds markup problems, not whether the message is useful, so keep the manual check too.

steps.do: List every red text class in the component folder to find the error color.
Confirm text-red-600 on white is about 4.83:1, which passes the 4.5:1 minimum for normal text.
Run pa11y against the error state with the WCAG2AA standard.
Flag any lighter red class, such as text-red-400, that would fall below 4.5:1 on white.

K-018689.example: TextField uses text-red-600 for the error message, which measures about 4.83:1 against white. pa11y reports no contrast errors on the error page.
K-018689.check: pa11y prints 0 errors with exit code 0, and the last grep prints no lines.
traps: A small model may pick text-red-400 because it looks softer, which fails 4.5:1 on white.
Contrast also depends on the background, so check the actual card or dark background the message sits on.
A 3:1 ratio is only the minimum for large text, not for a 14px error message.

steps.do: Run the spec that submits the form with the email field empty.
Confirm the component sets aria-invalid on the input when error is present.
Confirm the invalid state applies the Tailwind red border class.

K-018690.example: The spec clicks submit with the field empty and expects Email is required to appear. It also checks that the input has aria-invalid=true and the class border-red-600.
K-018690.check: Playwright prints 1 passed with exit code 0, and both greps print at least one matching line.
traps: Using the HTML required attribute alone skips the custom error text and the aria-invalid flag.
Building the class name from a string such as border-${color} means Tailwind never generates it, so write full class names in the source.

steps.do: Compile Tailwind from the entry stylesheet into the dist folder.
Count the compiled rules for the error border class.
Confirm the built CSS is under 20000 bytes.

K-018691.example: The entry file src/index.css contains the Tailwind import, and the build writes dist/index.css. The grep finds border-red-600 in the output, and wc reports 14820 bytes.
K-018691.check: grep -c prints 1 or more, and wc -c prints a number below 20000.
traps: Classes missing from the source files are not generated, so check the content paths in the config.
A v4 project needs the import line at the top of the entry CSS, not a tailwind.config.js content list.
Passing the build does not show that the variant is applied, so pair this check with a browser test.

steps.do: Create the menu component file.
Use $props to accept items as an array of objects with id and labelKey fields.
Set lang and dir on the root div, where dir is rtl when the locale is ar and ltr otherwise.
Render each label with t(item.labelKey) and never with a literal string.
Confirm no English literal remains in the component.
Run the RTL test, which sets the locale to ar, asserts lang="ar" and dir="rtl" on the root div, and asserts each menu button is at least 44px tall.

K-018692.example: With locale set to ar, the root div gets lang set to ar and dir set to rtl. The grep counts print 1, 1, 1 and then 0 for the literal 'Open menu', and the Playwright test exits 0.
K-018692.check: The grep -c commands print 1, 1, 1 and 0 in order, and npx playwright test exits 0 with the RTL test passing and every button measured at 44px or more.
traps: Put dir on the root menu element, not on a child, or the layout will not flip.
Forgetting the lang attribute breaks screen reader pronunciation and font selection.

steps.do: Read the terminal width the program will assume.
Read the terminal height the program will assume.
Reserve the last row for errors and cap each message at the column count minus 4 characters.
Find the existing error codes so the plan reuses them.

K-018693.example: tput cols prints 80 and tput lines prints 24, so the error row is row 23 counting from 0. Each message is capped at 76 characters.
K-018693.check: tput prints 80 and 24, and the plan names row 23 with a 76-character cap.
traps: Do not put the error row inside the item list area, or long lists will hide it.
Do not assume a size without running tput, because terminals differ.
Do not reuse an error code name that rg already finds in src.

steps.do: List the make targets to find the existing test target.
List the C test files already in the tree.
Write three cases into PLAN.md: zero items, error message set, and a normal list of 5 items.
Count the case lines in PLAN.md to confirm there are three.

K-018694.example: The plan lists the zero-item case, the error-message case, and the 5-item normal case. The grep count prints 3.
K-018694.check: grep prints 3, and make -n test shows the test target to extend.
traps: Do not add a fourth case by mistake, because the plan should cover exactly the three states.
Do not write the normal case without an item count, since 'normal' is not measurable.

steps.do: Read the current terminal width.
Read the current terminal height.
Write the minimum as 80 columns and 24 rows, with the message 'Terminal too small: need 80x24'.
Count the message bytes to confirm it fits in 80 columns.

K-018695.example: The plan sets the minimum to 80 by 24 and the message is 30 bytes. The wc command prints 30.
K-018695.check: wc prints 30, which is under the 80-column width, so the message fits on one row.
traps: Do not show the normal menu when the size check fails, because items will be cut off or wrap.
Do not write the minimum size without a number, since 'large enough' cannot be tested.

steps.do: Confirm src/app.html exists and find its head element.
Check that no theme attribute setter is already present.
Plan an inline script in head that reads localStorage key theme and sets data-theme on the html element.
Plan a fallback to matchMedia prefers-color-scheme dark when the key is missing or set to system.
Plan the script to run synchronously with no network request, within a 200ms budget.

K-018696.example: The inline script reads localStorage.getItem('theme') and sets data-theme to dark when the saved value is dark. It runs before the body renders, so the menu never paints in light mode first.
K-018696.check: The first grep prints one line number for the head tag, and the count prints 0 before the build stage and 1 after it, confirming exactly one inline setter exists.
traps: Small models often put the script in a Svelte component, which runs after first paint and causes the flash.
Do not forget that localStorage can throw in some private modes, so wrap the read in try and catch.
Do not add an external script file, because it loads too late to prevent the flash.

steps.do: Pick the light theme text and background pair, for example text #1f2937 on surface #ffffff.
Pick the dark theme text and background pair, for example text #e5e7eb on surface #161b22.
Confirm the axe-core package is installed so the verify stage can audit contrast.
Confirm Playwright is available to drive the menu in a browser.
State the thresholds: body text at least 4.5:1, focus ring at least 3:1, and menu items at least 44px tall.

K-018697.example: Light text #1f2937 on #ffffff is about 15.8:1, and dark text #e5e7eb on #161b22 is about 13:1, both above 4.5:1. The focus ring #2563eb on white is about 4.6:1, above the 3:1 non-text minimum.
K-018697.check: npx playwright --version prints a version number, and ls node_modules/@axe-core lists the axe-core folder, so the verify stage can run the contrast audit.
traps: Small models often assume dark text is just light text inverted and never measure the ratio.
Do not use the 3:1 threshold for body text, since normal text needs 4.5:1.
Do not skip the 44px minimum height for menu items, because touch targets fail below it.

steps.do: Find existing Playwright spec files outside node_modules.
Check that a Playwright config exists at the project root.
Write the planned check that toggling the theme sets data-theme to dark within 200ms.
Write the planned axe check that reports zero serious contrast violations on the menu in both themes.
Name the planned test file menu-theme and confirm it lists the expected tests.

K-018698.example: The planned test opens the menu, sets the theme to dark, and expects the html data-theme attribute to equal dark within 200ms. The axe run must report 0 serious contrast violations in both themes.
K-018698.check: After the build stage, npx playwright test menu-theme --list prints a total of 2 tests in 1 file, and before that it reports no matching tests.
traps: Small models often run the full test suite instead of the single menu test, which hides the result they need.
Do not claim a test passed during the plan stage, since nothing is built yet.
Do not take screenshots without a fixed viewport, because the pixel diff becomes noisy.

steps.do: Go to the crate directory.
Find every call to terminal.draw in the main loop.
Add a bool field named dirty to App, set it to true only in the key handler after selected changes, and wrap terminal.draw in an if app.dirty check.
Replace the zero timeout poll with event::poll(Duration::from_millis(50)) so the loop sleeps between events instead of spinning.
Write a test named redraw_skips_when_clean that sets dirty to false and asserts the draw counter stays at 0.
Run that test alone.

K-018699.example: After a key press moves selected from 0 to 1, dirty becomes true and one draw happens, then dirty is reset to false. With no input for 1 second, the draw counter stays at 0 across 20 poll timeouts of 50ms.
K-018699.check: cargo test prints 'test redraw_skips_when_clean ... ok' and 'test result: ok. 1 passed'.
traps: Setting dirty on every loop tick defeats the skip, so set it only on input.
A poll timeout of 0 makes the loop spin and use full CPU.
Reset dirty to false after drawing, or the screen redraws forever.

steps.do: Go to the crate directory.
List the pane render functions so you know their names.
In the draw function, use a match on app.selected and call only the matching render function for the body area.
Keep each pane's data as plain structs in App, not as built widgets, so switching tabs does not rebuild widgets.
Run the test that counts pane renders.
Check that the crate still compiles with no warnings.

K-018700.example: With selected set to 1, the match calls render_logs only, so the counter for render_files and render_help stays at 0 for that frame. cargo test then reports one passing test.
K-018700.check: cargo test shows 'test lazy_tab_renders_one_pane ... ok' and cargo check ends with Finished with no warning lines.
traps: Drawing all three panes and clipping the result wastes work every frame.
A match with a wildcard arm can hide a missing pane, so match every index explicitly.
Storing built widgets in App means rebuilding them whenever data changes, so store plain data.

steps.do: Go to the crate directory.
Add a test in tests/tab_perf.rs that starts an Instant, calls the next-tab method 1000 times, and asserts elapsed is under Duration::from_millis(200).
Run the timing test in release mode because debug timings are not representative.
List the release output directory to confirm the test build artifacts exist.

K-018701.example: The test calls App::next_tab 1000 times and records an elapsed time of 3ms in release mode, well under the 200ms limit. The printed line shows the measured duration so the number is visible.
K-018701.check: Output includes 'test tab_switch_budget ... ok' and the printed elapsed value is below 200ms.
traps: Running without --release measures unoptimized code and gives false failures.
Assert a time budget, not an exact duration, because machine load varies.
Calling next_tab once is too short to measure, so loop 1000 times.

steps.do: Go to the crate directory.
Find every place that writes to app.selected.
Write next_tab as selected = (selected + 1) % TAB_TITLES.len() and prev_tab as selected = (selected + TAB_TITLES.len() - 1) % TAB_TITLES.len().
Run clippy with warnings denied to catch unused code and index mistakes.
Run the wrap test that presses next on the last tab and expects index 0.

K-018702.example: With TAB_TITLES of length 3 and selected at 2, next_tab sets selected to 0. With selected at 0, prev_tab sets selected to 2 because (0 + 3 - 1) % 3 is 2.
K-018702.check: cargo clippy ends with Finished and no warning lines, and cargo test shows 'test wrap_selection ... ok'.
traps: Forgetting the modulo lets selected reach 3 and panics on TAB_TITLES index access.
In prev_tab, subtracting 1 from 0 underflows an unsigned usize, so add the length first.
Hardcoding 3 breaks when a tab is added, so use TAB_TITLES.len().

steps.do: Find where the program calls keypad to enable function keys.
Write ESCDELAY as 25 milliseconds in the launch plan.
Confirm the launch environment passes the delay value through.
Check that 25 ms is under the 200 ms response budget.

K-018703.example: The plan sets ESCDELAY to 25 ms so Escape is read within 25 ms instead of the default 1000 ms. printenv prints 25, and python3 prints True.
K-018703.check: printenv prints 25, python3 prints True, and the plan states 25 ms as the delay.
traps: Do not use the default ESCDELAY of 1000 ms, which makes Escape feel stuck after an error.
Do not set ESCDELAY after initscr runs, because ncurses reads it at startup.

steps.do: Check whether src/app.css already defines custom properties on :root.
Confirm which layout imports the global stylesheet.
Confirm no menu tokens exist yet. The printed number must be 0.
Write the five planned token names: --menu-bg, --menu-fg, --menu-border, --menu-hover, and --menu-focus. Pick text and background pairs that reach at least 4.5:1 contrast.
Plan the dark values under the selector [data-theme='dark'] on the html element in src/app.css, not inside the component. Check that the dark text and background pairs also reach at least 4.5:1.

K-018704.example: The plan sets --menu-bg to #ffffff under :root and #161b22 under [data-theme='dark'] in src/app.css. Menu.svelte only reads var(--menu-bg), so its markup never changes between themes. The text pair #1f2937 on #ffffff is about 14:1, which passes 4.5:1.
K-018704.check: The plan lists exactly 5 token names and 10 declarations, 5 under :root and 5 under the dark selector. Step 3 prints 0 until the build stage, and each text and background pair in both themes reaches at least 4.5:1.
traps: Small models often put dark colors inside the Svelte component with a media query, which splits the theme across files.
Do not use another framework's theme API, such as a React context, in a Svelte app.
Keep all token names under one --menu- prefix so they are easy to search.

steps.do: Search the table widget folder for literal fontSize values.
Confirm the table file reads the theme's textTheme instead.
Run the token test that checks header and body styles against the ThemeData values.

K-018705.example: The fontSize grep must print nothing and exit with code 1, while the textTheme grep must print lines such as lib/widgets/table/app_data_table.dart:42 with textTheme.bodyMedium. The test asserts headerStyle equals textTheme.titleSmall and cellStyle equals textTheme.bodyMedium.
K-018705.check: The fontSize grep prints no lines, the textTheme grep prints at least two lines, and flutter test prints All tests passed!
traps: A grep with no matches is the passing result here, so do not add fontSize to make output appear.
Compare against the ThemeData values in the test, not against TextStyle defaults.
Literal numbers such as 14.0 in a helper file still count as hardcoded.

steps.do: Format the token and table files in place.
Run the analyzer on the design folder and the table folder.
Run the unit test that checks AppTokens lerp and copyWith.

K-018706.example: AppTokens in lib/design/tokens.dart declares tableRowHeight as 48.0 and tableBodyFontSize as 14.0. The lerp test calls AppTokens.light.lerp(AppTokens.dark, 0.5) and expects tableRowHeight to equal 48.0.
K-018706.check: dart analyze prints No issues found!, and flutter test prints All tests passed!
traps: A ThemeExtension that skips overriding copyWith or lerp fails at theme switch time, not at compile time.
dart format rewrites files, so run analyze again after formatting.
Do not use dynamic in the token class to silence an error.

steps.do: Run the contrast test that computes WCAG ratios for each table text and background pair.
Confirm the contrast test sets the 4.5 threshold.
List the color tokens so each one can be matched to a tested pair.

K-018707.example: Body text #1F1F1F on the striped row #F5F5F5 gives a ratio of about 16.1:1. Header text #FFFFFF on #1A4D8F gives about 8.9:1, and the test fails if any pair falls below 4.5.
K-018707.check: flutter test prints All tests passed!, the threshold grep prints at least one line containing 4.5, and every Color token in the output appears in a tested pair.
traps: Compute ratios from relative luminance, not from averages of RGB values.
Test the stripe color as well as the base row color, since both sit under body text.
A 3:1 threshold applies only where the design doc says so; the default is 4.5:1.

steps.do: Run the widget test that pumps the table with the text scaler set to 2.0.
Confirm the test file uses TextScaler.linear with 2.0.
Run every table test to catch overflow in other tests.

K-018708.example: The test wraps DataTable in a MediaQuery with textScaler set to TextScaler.linear(2.0) on a 360 by 640 logical pixel surface. It fails if tester.takeException returns a RenderFlex overflow error.
K-018708.check: The scale test prints All tests passed!, the grep prints one line containing TextScaler.linear(2.0), and the folder run prints All tests passed! with no RenderFlex overflowed messages.
traps: An 800 pixel wide test surface hides overflow that a 360 pixel phone shows.
textScaleFactor is deprecated, so use textScaler with TextScaler.linear.
Wrapping cells in FittedBox hides overflow by shrinking the text, which is the wrong fix.

steps.do: Run the golden test for table typography in light and dark themes.
List the golden PNG files stored for the table.
Check the golden test loads the real app font so glyphs are not placeholder boxes.

K-018709.example: The golden test renders the table at text scale 1.0 and 1.5 in light and dark themes, then compares each frame with matchesGoldenFile. The listing should show table_body_dark.png, table_body_light.png, table_header_dark.png, and table_header_light.png.
K-018709.check: flutter test prints All tests passed!, ls -1 prints exactly four PNG names, and the FontLoader grep prints one line.
traps: Running flutter test --update-goldens without reviewing the diff hides real regressions.
Without FontLoader the test uses the Ahem font, so screenshots show blocks and look correct when they are not.
Goldens rendered at a different devicePixelRatio cannot be compared with the stored files.

steps.do: Search the table code for the tabular figures font feature.
Run the test that asserts numeric cell styles include the tabular figures feature.
Confirm numeric cells are aligned to the end of the column.

K-018710.example: NumericCell sets fontFeatures to a list holding FontFeature.tabularFigures() and sets textAlign to TextAlign.end. The test renders 1,111.00 and 8.00 in the same column and checks both cells have the same digit advance width.
K-018710.check: The first grep prints at least one line containing tabularFigures, flutter test prints All tests passed!, and the second grep prints at least one line.
traps: Some fonts ignore the tabular feature, so confirm the font in pubspec.yaml supports tabular digits.
TextAlign.center on numbers breaks column alignment, so use TextAlign.end.
Typing the raw tag string into a feature list invites typos, so use FontFeature.tabularFigures().

steps.do: Set each tab button label frame to at least 44 points wide and 44 points tall.
Add contentShape with Rectangle so the whole frame is tappable, including empty padding.
Write a UI test class named TabHitTargetTests that asserts each tab button frame is at least 44 points in width and height.
Run the hit target test class on the simulator.
List every frame call in the tab bar file to check that none sets a size below 44.

K-018711.example: Each Button label has .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44) and .contentShape(Rectangle()). The UI test asserts that button.frame.height is at least 44 for all four tabs.
K-018711.check: xcodebuild reports TabHitTargetTests passed with 0 failures and ends with ** TEST SUCCEEDED **.
traps: A 44 point icon is not the same as a 44 point tap area, so the frame must be on the tappable view.
SwiftUI measures in points, not pixels, so do not double the value for @2x or @3x screens.

steps.do: Use semantic text styles such as font caption instead of fixed point sizes for tab labels.
Search the tab sources for fixed font sizes, which ignore Dynamic Type.
Set app.launchArguments in the UI test to force the largest accessibility content size before app.launch.
Run the Dynamic Type UI test class on the simulator.

K-018712.example: The test appends -UIPreferredContentSizeCategoryName and UICTContentSizeCategoryAccessibilityExtraExtraExtraLarge to app.launchArguments, then asserts that the Library tab label exists and its frame height is above 22 points. grep -rn finds no matches for fixed sizes.
K-018712.check: grep prints no lines and DynamicTypeTabTests passes with 0 failures.
traps: A fixed font size such as system size 12 ignores the user's Dynamic Type setting.
Launch arguments must be set before app.launch is called, or the test runs at the default size.

steps.do: Add accessibilityIdentifier with a fixed string such as tab-library to each tab item.
Write a test that taps the Library tab and asserts that its isSelected property is true.
List the identifier lines to confirm there is one per tab.
Run the tab selection test class on the simulator.

K-018713.example: The test calls app.tabBars.buttons['tab-library'].tap() and then asserts that app.tabBars.buttons['tab-library'].isSelected is true. The grep lists four matching lines, one per tab.
K-018713.check: grep prints exactly four lines and TabSelectionTests passes with 0 failures.
traps: Use the identifier rather than the visible title, because titles change with localization.
Do not use sleep for timing; use waitForExistence with a timeout of 2 seconds instead.

steps.do: List the color sets for the tab colors in the asset catalog.
Compute the contrast ratio of each label color against its background and confirm text reaches at least 4.5:1.
Confirm that icons reach at least 3:1 against their background, since non-text graphics use a lower floor.
Confirm the snapshot baseline images exist for the light and dark tab renderings.
Run the snapshot test class, which compares light and dark renderings against the stored images.

K-018714.example: Selected label #0A5FD6 on white gives 5.8:1 and unselected label #767680 on white gives 4.6:1, both above 4.5:1. The snapshot test diffs the light and dark renderings against the stored PNG files.
K-018714.check: find lists each colorset path, ls lists the baseline PNGs, and TabsSnapshotTests ends with ** TEST SUCCEEDED **, with every text ratio at 4.5:1 or higher.
traps: Do not use color alone to show selection, because the trait and a visible indicator must also change.
Do not judge contrast by eye, and do not forget that dark mode uses a separate variant in the color set.

steps.do: Confirm the stylesheet has a reduced-motion media query block.
Run the Playwright spec that emulates reduced motion in the browser context.
Confirm the output reports 1 passed with zero failed tests.

K-018715.example: grep prints 12:@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) followed by a .bar rule with transition-duration 0ms in chart.css. The spec sets reducedMotion to reduce and expects each .bar computed transition-duration to be 0s.
K-018715.check: grep prints at least one match; Playwright prints 1 passed with no failures.
traps: Small models check for the media query but never test it in a browser, and a grep cannot show the computed value.
Transitions added inline from JavaScript are not covered by the stylesheet block.
Run the browser test, not just the grep.

steps.do: List the dashoffset rules and animation declared for the line path.
Run the spec that waits 1200ms and reads the path computed stroke-dashoffset.
Confirm the assertion for final dashoffset 0px passed.

K-018716.example: chart.css sets .line-path to stroke-dasharray 840 and stroke-dashoffset 840 with animation draw 1s ease-out forwards. The spec waits 1200ms and expects computed stroke-dashoffset 0px, so a value of 840px means the animation never ran.
K-018716.check: grep shows animation-fill-mode forwards or the animation shorthand includes forwards; Playwright prints 1 passed for the expect 0px assertion.
traps: The dasharray must match the real path length or the line looks partly drawn.
Checking before the animation duration ends gives a false failure.
Without forwards the line snaps back to 840px after the animation ends.

steps.do: Print the keyframes block that drives the bar grow animation.
Run the spec that waits for animations to finish, then measures each bar height.
Confirm the tallest bar measures 240px for data value 240 within 1px.

K-018717.example: The spec sets data value 240 and expects the .bar boundingBox height to equal 240px within 1px after 800ms. A measured height of 0px means the 100% keyframe step sets scaleY 0 or fill-mode is missing.
K-018717.check: grep shows a @keyframes grow block whose 100% step sets the final size, and Playwright prints 1 passed.
traps: Measuring before the animation ends gives a height below the data value.
The final size belongs in the 100% step, not the 0% step.
Allow 1px tolerance because subpixel rounding changes the measured height.

steps.do: List every animation duration declared in the chart stylesheet with its line number.
Run the spec that records the last animationend time across all bars.
Confirm every declared duration is 600ms or less and the spec reports the last animationend under 600ms.

K-018718.example: grep prints 12:animation-duration: 450ms, so each bar grows in 450ms. With a 100ms stagger across 4 bars, the last bar ends at 750ms, which breaks the 600ms budget and needs a shorter duration or stagger.
K-018718.check: grep prints every duration at 600ms or less and Playwright prints 1 passed.
traps: Stagger delays add to total time, so the last bar's delay plus its duration is what counts.
Compare the last animationend, not the first.
Mixing seconds and milliseconds is a common error: 0.45s equals 450ms.

steps.do: Create the custom tab bar file.
Make each tab a Button and add accessibilityAddTraits with isSelected only when its value equals the current selection.
Give each Button an accessibilityLabel with the tab name, separate from the icon.
Count the accessibilityLabel lines. The count must equal the number of tabs, which is 4 for Home, Search, Library, and Profile.
Count the isSelected lines to confirm the trait is set by one conditional, not on every button. The count must be exactly 1.
Build the target to confirm it compiles.

K-018719.example: Inside a ForEach over TabItem.allCases, the Button uses accessibilityAddTraits(selection == item ? .isSelected : []), so only the active tab carries the trait. grep -c 'isSelected' finds one matching line and grep -c 'accessibilityLabel' finds 4.
K-018719.check: grep -c 'isSelected' prints exactly 1, grep -c 'accessibilityLabel' prints exactly 4, and xcodebuild ends with ** BUILD SUCCEEDED **.
traps: Do not add isSelected unconditionally to every button, since every tab would then announce as selected.
Do not set the label only on the image, because VoiceOver then reads the icon name instead of the tab name.

steps.do: Build the static chart page into the dist folder.
In a second terminal, serve dist on port 8080 and leave it running.
Run Lighthouse on the served chart page and save the JSON report.
Read the cumulative layout shift value from the report.

K-018720.example: jq prints 0.02 for chart.html, which is under the 0.1 limit. A value of 0.25 would mean bars or labels move the page during the animation.
K-018720.check: lh-chart.json exists and jq prints a number below 0.1, such as 0.02.
traps: Lighthouse needs the page served over http, not opened as a file path.
Small models often report the performance score instead of the CLS number.
CLS above 0.1 usually means the animation changes layout, so animate transform instead of top or height.

steps.do: Set the nav aria-label to the Arabic word for navigation in ar/index.html.
Confirm the Arabic nav has exactly one aria-label attribute.
Add a font rule for Arabic text using the :lang selector in styles/nav.css.
Confirm the Arabic font rule exists in the stylesheet.
Check that the nav has no color-contrast violation at 4.5:1 on the Arabic page.

K-018721.example: The rule :lang(ar) { font-family: 'Noto Naskh Arabic', serif; } applies to any element marked lang="ar". The axe run on port 8080 must report zero color-contrast violations.
K-018721.check: The grep prints 1, the rg prints one line with :lang(ar), and axe reports 0 color-contrast violations.
traps: Using font-family without a fallback leaves some Arabic glyphs unrendered.
Choosing nav text colors that pass on white but fail on the nav background.
Forgetting to serve the page on localhost:8080 before running axe.

steps.do: Wrap the brand name in the nav with a span that has translate set to no.
Confirm the brand span carries translate no in index.html.
Confirm the French page has the same brand span.
Run axe on the French page with the WCAG 2 AA rules.

K-018722.example: The markup Acme keeps the brand name fixed while the link words change. Each page should print a count of 1 and axe should report zero violations.
K-018722.check: Each grep prints 1 and axe reports 0 violations.
traps: Adding translate to the whole nav instead of the brand span blocks translation of link text.
Forgetting that translate is an attribute and not a CSS property.
Leaving the brand name out of the French page makes it inconsistent.

steps.do: Create the tests folder for the spec file.
Create the Playwright spec file for the nav.
Write a test that loads /ar/ and checks each nav link box height is at least 44px.
Confirm the spec file calls boundingBox at least once.
Run the spec file against the served Arabic page.

K-018723.example: The test loads http://localhost:8080/ar/ and reads each a.nav-link with boundingBox, expecting height 44 or more. The run output shows 1 passed for a page where every link is 48px tall.
K-018723.check: The grep prints 1 or more and the playwright run prints 1 passed with exit code 0.
traps: Measuring the link text instead of the clickable box leaves padding out of the height.
Testing the English page only misses RTL layout bugs.
Skipping the 44px minimum because the links look large enough.

steps.do: Check the installed Tailwind version to pick the right config and variant syntax.
Define three states: idle shows content, loading shows a skeleton, error shows a message.
Set the skeleton to appear only after 200ms so fast responses do not flicker.
Create the plan file that will record these decisions.
Confirm the plan file records the 200ms delay number.

K-018724.example: The version command prints 3.4.1, so the plan uses tailwind.config.js and v3 variant names. The plan sets the skeleton delay to 200ms and the fetch timeout to 8000ms.
K-018724.check: npx tailwindcss -v prints a version such as 3.4.1, and grep -n 200ms prints a line number with the delay number from the plan.
traps: Small models often show the skeleton instantly, which causes flicker on fast loads. Pick a delay number and write it down.
Do not guess the Tailwind version from memory. Read it with the version command first.

steps.do: Find existing uses of aria-selected in the source to match the current pattern.
Decide that the tabpanel gets aria-busy set to true while loading, and the active tab keeps aria-selected set to true.
Confirm Tailwind 3.2 or later is installed, because aria-busy variants need it.
Note the variant to use on the panel, which is aria-busy:opacity-50.

K-018725.example: npm ls tailwindcss prints tailwindcss@3.4.1, so aria-busy variants are available. The tabpanel div in SettingsTabs.tsx gets aria-busy=true during the fetch and drops opacity to 50 percent through the aria-busy:opacity-50 class.
K-018725.check: npm ls tailwindcss prints a version of 3.2 or higher, and the plan lists aria-busy on the tabpanel, not on the tab button.
traps: Small models often put aria-busy on the tab button instead of the panel. The panel is the element whose content is loading.
Do not drop aria-selected while loading, because screen readers need to know which tab is active.

steps.do: Check whether any existing skeleton already uses motion-reduce classes.
Choose three skeleton rows, each with h-4 w-full rounded bg-gray-200, where h-4 is 1rem.
Set the pulse to animate-pulse motion-reduce:animate-none so reduced-motion users see a static block.
Confirm the tailwind config defines no custom animation that would conflict with animate-pulse.
Set each tab button to h-11, which is 2.75rem or 44px, so the tap target meets the minimum.

K-018726.example: The grep for motion-reduce prints no files, so the skeleton will be new. The plan uses three rows of h-4 at 1rem each and tab buttons of h-11 at 44px.
K-018726.check: grep -rln motion-reduce exits 1 with no output if no file uses it, and the plan lists the h-11 tab height as 44px.
traps: Small models often omit motion-reduce, so the pulse keeps animating for users who asked for less motion. Always pair animate-pulse with motion-reduce:animate-none.
Do not pick a tab height below 44px. Write the exact class and its pixel value in the plan.

steps.do: Count the existing Playwright tests so the new tests can be added to the same suite.
Plan arrow key focus movement that skips disabled loading tabs.
Plan the loading label as text-gray-600 on bg-white, which is about 7.5:1 contrast and above the 4.5:1 minimum.
Plan an axe accessibility scan of the settings page while loading.

K-018727.example: The list command prints Total 12 tests, so the new tests go in the same suite. The plan uses text-gray-600 on bg-white for the loading label, which is above 4.5:1, and rejects text-gray-400 on white at about 2.5:1.
K-018727.check: npx playwright test --list prints a Total line with a test count, and the plan states a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for the loading label.
traps: Small models often choose text-gray-400 for loading labels, which fails the 4.5:1 minimum on white. Calculate the ratio before picking a color.
Do not plan keyboard support that moves focus onto a disabled tab. Arrow keys should skip it.

steps.do: Find existing fetch calls inside the tab components.
List the tab component files that fetch data on mount.
Decide to keep loaded panels mounted and hide inactive ones with the hidden class, instead of unmounting them.
Set the fetch timeout to 8000ms and show the error state when it expires.
Count the hidden class uses in the components to see how many panels stay mounted.

K-018728.example: The fetch search finds one call in SettingsTabs.tsx, so only that panel needs caching. The plan keeps loaded panels mounted with the hidden class and sets the timeout to 8000ms.
K-018728.check: grep -rn fetch prints the file and line of each fetch call, and the plan states an 8000ms timeout and a hidden-class strategy.
traps: Small models often unmount panels on tab switch, which refetches data on every click. Keep loaded panels mounted and hide them.
Without a timeout a loading tab can spin forever. Always set a number such as 8000ms and plan the error state for it.

steps.do: Find where the existing code polls for input events so you know the current loop timing.
Record the spinner timing decision in the plan file: show the spinner only after 200ms, and advance one frame every 80ms.
Confirm both timing values appear in the plan file.

K-018729.example: The plan says the spinner appears after 200ms of loading and advances every 80ms. grep -n then prints two matching lines, one with each value.
K-018729.check: grep -n prints one line containing 200ms and one line containing 80ms, each with a line number.
traps: Do not pick a delay of 0ms, because the spinner will flash on every fast load.
Do not set the tick below 50ms, because the redraw will cost more CPU than the animation is worth.
Do not forget that poll timeout must be at least as short as the tick.

steps.do: Create the tests directory if it does not exist.
Create the empty test file that will hold the loading timeout test.
Record in the plan file that a load fails after 5000ms and the test is named menu_loading_timeout.
Confirm the timeout value is in the plan file.
Confirm the test file exists and lists zero tests before the build stage.

K-018730.example: The plan says a load moves to Failed after 5000ms. cargo test --list then prints 0 tests, which is correct before the build stage writes menu_loading_timeout.
K-018730.check: rg -n prints a line with 5000. cargo test --list prints a line containing 0 tests.
traps: Do not set the timeout in seconds and then write 5000 in the plan, because the code must use milliseconds.
Do not put the test in src/ui/menu.rs when Cargo runs integration tests from tests/.
Do not treat a 0-test list as a failure; it is the expected state at the plan stage.

steps.do: Create a folder named ar for the Arabic pages.
Create the Arabic home page file.
Write the html element with lang set to ar and dir set to rtl as the first element in ar/index.html.
Confirm the html element carries lang ar and dir rtl.
Confirm the file has exactly one html element.
Run axe on the served Arabic page and confirm no contrast violations.

K-018731.example: The file ar/index.html starts with <html lang="ar" dir="rtl">, so screen readers read Arabic and the nav mirrors to the right. The first grep prints 1, the second grep prints 1, and axe exits with code 0 and reports 0 violations, so nav text meets the 4.5:1 contrast minimum.
K-018731.check: The first grep prints 1, the second grep prints 1, and the axe run exits with code 0 and reports 0 violations, with nav text at least 4.5:1 contrast.
traps: Putting dir on the nav instead of the html element leaves the page text direction wrong.
Using lang="ar-SA" in one file and lang="ar" in another makes checks inconsistent.
Writing two html elements in one file breaks the document structure.

steps.do: List every physical margin property left in the nav stylesheet.
Replace each physical property with its logical equivalent, such as margin-inline-start in place of margin-left.
Confirm no physical margin property remains in the nav stylesheet.
Confirm the logical property is present in the nav stylesheet.
Confirm each nav link has a minimum height of 44px.

K-018732.example: The rule .nav-link { margin-inline-start: 1rem; min-height: 44px; } gives 16px of space on the start side, which is the left in LTR and the right in RTL, and a 44px tap target. After the change, the first rg prints no lines, the last rg prints the rule line, and the third rg prints at least one line.
K-018732.check: The third command prints no output, the fourth command prints at least one line with margin-inline-start, and the fifth command prints at least one line with min-height: 44px.
traps: Mixing margin-left with margin-inline-start in the same rule causes unpredictable spacing in RTL.
Changing only the margin and not the padding leaves the nav items uneven.
Assuming rtl alone flips the layout without using logical properties.
Setting a 44px height on the nav container but not on each link leaves small tap targets.

steps.do: List every file that renders a tablist role.
Confirm Tailwind scans those files through the content globs.
Count matches of the animate-pulse utility in each source file.
Check that tab transitions use the 200ms duration class by finding duration-200 in the source.
Create the planning folder for the tabs loading work.

K-018733.example: The first command prints src/components/SettingsTabs.tsx, so that file is the one tablist to plan around. The count command prints 0 for that file, which means no skeleton exists yet and one must be planned. The duration command prints a line with duration-200 if the tab transition is 200ms, or prints nothing if it is not.
K-018733.check: grep -rln prints at least one file path and exits 0. grep -rc prints a count for each file, with 0 meaning no skeleton yet. grep -rnF duration-200 prints matching lines with the 200ms class, and a line naming duration-200 confirms the 200ms number.
traps: Small models often skip the content check, so a new class like animate-pulse may never be generated. Always confirm the content globs cover the tab files.
Do not assume a tab file exists because the component name suggests it. Run the grep first.
Tailwind only generates classes it finds in scanned files, so a duration-200 match outside the content globs does not mean the class is compiled.

steps.do: Create the docs directory if it does not exist.
Create the plan file that will hold the state list.
Write four bullet lines into the plan file, one each for Idle, Loading, Ready, and Failed, using an editor or the Write tool.
Count the bullet lines in the plan file to confirm there are exactly four states.
Lint the plan file with markdownlint to confirm it is well-formed Markdown.

K-018734.example: After writing the file, grep -c prints 4 for the four bullets. markdownlint-cli2 reports 0 errors. Each bullet names one state and the key the user presses in that state.

K-018751.example: The plan says errors appear after blur, styled with user-invalid:text-red-700 at about 6.5:1 contrast, and the email error has id email-error referenced by aria-describedby.
